info.description:
Read-only access to the yfin market data warehouse: symbols, price bars,
corporate actions, financial statements, analyst coverage, holdings,
news, discovery results and the sector/industry taxonomy.

## Getting a token

Authentication is the OAuth2 **client credentials** grant. Send your
client id and secret as HTTP Basic to `/oauth/token`; you get a bearer
token valid for 15 minutes.

```
curl -u "$CLIENT_ID:$CLIENT_SECRET" \
     -d grant_type=client_credentials \
     https://<host>/oauth/token
```

Ask for fewer scopes than you hold with `-d scope="bars:read"`. The token
carries what was granted, and the response says so.

Revocation is immediate: rotating a secret or narrowing a scope stops the
tokens already issued, without waiting for them to expire.

## Paging

Collections return `{"data": [...], "next_cursor": ...}`. Pass
`next_cursor` back as `?cursor=` to get the next page, and stop when it
comes back `null`. There is no `offset`: on tables with hundreds of
millions of rows an offset gets slower the deeper you go and can skip
rows while data is being written.

A cursor belongs to the query that produced it. Change the interval, the
range or a filter and it is refused with `422 invalid_cursor` rather than
quietly returning the wrong page.

## Reading values

**Numbers arrive as strings.** Prices and share counts are stored as
exact decimals; sending them as JSON numbers would round them on the way
out. Parse them with a decimal type, not a float.

**Two different dates.** `ts_utc` is always UTC. `session_date` is the
exchange's trading session; `local_date` is the bar's local calendar day.
They are not interchangeable -- a bar late in the local evening can
belong to the next session.

**Ranges are half-open.** `from` is included, `to` is not, so consecutive
pages never overlap.

**Bars default to regular hours.** Pass `session=all` for intraday
extended-hours bars. The default is deliberate: mixing them into a
regular series silently distorts anything computed from it.

## Limits

Every response carries `RateLimit-*` for the per-second budget and
`X-Quota-*` for the monthly one. A `429` says which limit was hit in its
`type` field and how long to wait in `Retry-After`. Requests that fail
with a `5xx` are not counted against your quota.

Errors are [RFC 9457](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9457) problem
documents, except on `/oauth/token`, which uses the OAuth2 error shape
its own standard requires.

## Resources

Everything below is served by `GET /v1/datasets/{name}`, where the
name is the first column. `symbol` says whether the resource is
per-symbol: *required* means you must pass `?symbol=`, *optional*
means you may browse without one. Time-ordered resources come
newest first.

Requires the `reference:read` scope.

| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| `earnings_dates` | Past and upcoming earnings dates. | required | — |
| `earnings_estimate` | Consensus earnings estimates by period. | required | — |
| `earnings_history` | Reported versus estimated EPS, by quarter. | required | — |
| `economic_calendar` | Scheduled macroeconomic events by region. | — | `region` |
| `eps_revisions` | Counts of upward and downward EPS revisions. | required | — |
| `eps_trend` | Consensus EPS estimate as it moved over time. | required | — |
| `growth_estimates` | Consensus growth estimates by period. | required | — |
| `ipo_calendar` | IPO pricings, filings and withdrawals. | optional | `action` |
| `recommendations` | Buy/hold/sell recommendation counts by period. | required | — |
| `revenue_estimate` | Consensus revenue estimates by period. | required | — |
| `sec_filing_exhibits` | Documents attached to a filing. | required | `exhibit_type` |
| `sec_filings` | SEC filings, newest first. | required | `filing_type` |
| `shares_full` | Shares outstanding over time. | required | — |
| `splits_calendar` | Announced stock splits and their payable dates. | optional | — |

Requires the `holders:read` scope.

| `fund_weightings` | Sector, asset-class and bond-rating weightings. | required | `category` |
| `insider_purchases` | Aggregated insider buying and selling. | required | — |
| `insider_roster_holders` | Insiders on record and the shares they hold. | required | — |
| `insider_transactions` | Individual insider transactions. | required | — |
| `institutional_holders` | Institutional holders and their reported positions. | required | — |
| `major_holders` | Ownership split between insiders and institutions. | required | — |
| `mutualfund_holders` | Mutual fund holders and their reported positions. | required | — |

## news

Requires the `news:read` scope.

| name | what it is | symbol | filters |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

## domains

Requires the `domains:read` scope.

| name | what it is | symbol | filters |

get.description:
Bars for one symbol.

`session` applies to intraday intervals only, and defaults to
`regular`. That default is accident prevention: extended-hours bars
mixed into a regular series corrupt every indicator computed from it,
invisibly. Above daily the flag has no meaning, so passing it there is
rejected rather than ignored.

parameters.description: Bar size. Intraday intervals are routed to the intraday tables, `1d` to the daily one and `1wk`/`1mo` to the periodic one; each carries its own cap on how wide a range may be asked for.
parameters.name: interval

get.description:
Line items for one statement.

`statement` and `freq` are both required, and that is a performance
contract rather than a stylistic choice: `financial_facts` is keyed on
(symbol, statement, freq, period_end, item_key), so without them the
query cannot use the leading columns of its own primary key.
